stimulus.description: Mean angle of stem curvature toward the light source after 24 hours (mean ± 2SE) for each group of bean seedlings

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A student investigates how the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot affects the bean seedlings' response. Identify the independent variable in the investigation.
parts.model_answer: The independent variable is the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the independent variable
required_elements: wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot
optional_phrases: the levels tested: white light (control), red light, blue light
alt_solutions: the factor the experimenter deliberately changed
the manipulated variable
common_errors: names the measured response (dependent variable)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the group that served as the control in the investigation, and explain why a control group is needed.
parts.model_answer: The control group was the white light (control) group, which provides a baseline for comparison.

rubric_rows.criterion: Names the control group and states it provides a baseline/comparison for the effect of the variable
alt_solutions: the group that does not receive the treatment of interest
the reference group used for comparison
common_errors: names a treated group as the control
says a control makes the results larger

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: State a null hypothesis for the investigation.
parts.model_answer: There is no difference in the angle of stem curvature toward the light source among the groups; the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot has no effect.

rubric_rows.criterion: States no effect or no difference in the dependent variable among the groups
alt_solutions: the independent variable does not affect the dependent variable
any differences are due to chance
common_errors: states a prediction of a difference instead of no effect

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A student claims that blue light increases the angle of stem curvature toward the light source compared with white light (control). Using the data in the table, support the student's claim.
parts.model_answer: blue light: 42.1 ± 3.0 versus control 3.9 ± 3.0; the ±2SE intervals do not overlap, so the difference is statistically supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: Cites the group means and notes the error bars (±2SE) do not overlap (the difference is real)
alt_solutions: the means differ by more than the variability
the +/-2SE intervals are separated
common_errors: cites the means but ignores the error bars
claims causation without comparing to the control

stimulus.description: Mean oxygen released in 2 minutes (milliliters) ± 2SE for a catalase-catalyzed reaction at three levels of temperature

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Based on the data, describe the relationship between temperature and the oxygen released in 2 minutes across the three levels.
parts.model_answer: The oxygen released in 2 minutes peaks across the levels (4.9, 17.2, 2.6).

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the trend using the values (or direction) from the table
alt_solutions: increases then decreases
rises then falls
highest at the middle level
describes the direction of change between consecutive levels using the values
common_errors: describes only one pair of levels

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes from 10 °C to 37 °C. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Percent change with work shown (answer)
alt_solutions: percent change = (new - old) / old x 100
common_errors: divides by the new value
forgets to multiply by 100

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Using the error bars (±2SE), identify the pair of levels, if any, for which the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes is not statistically different.
parts.model_answer: Answer: none of the pairs.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the pair whose ±2SE intervals overlap (or states none) (answer)
alt_solutions: the pair whose error bars overlap
none of the pairs differ
common_errors: compares only the means

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: A student claims that oxygen released in 2 minutes is greatest at 37 °C. Use the data to support the claim and describe what the error bars indicate about it.
parts.model_answer: 17.2 ± 2.02 at 37 °C is higher than the other levels; the ±2SE intervals do not overlap.

rubric_rows.criterion: Cites the highest mean and states what the non-overlap/overlap of error bars shows (support)
alt_solutions: the error bars do not overlap so the difference is real
higher mean with separated intervals
common_errors: cites the highest mean but does not discuss variability
